target.title: fix(line): dripping inbound media downloads hang past setup timeout
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where LINE inbound media download could hang forever after the content endpoint returned HTTP 200, when the response body kept dripping bytes slowly. `fetchLineContentWhenReady` cleared its 15s `AbortController` after headers returned `Readable.fromWeb(response.body)`, leaving no wall-clock bound on the Node stream consumed by `saveMediaStream` — a slow-drip CDN body would keep inbound media handling alive indefinitely.

## Why This Change Was Made

On current `main`, readiness owns a 15s `AbortController` inside `fetchLineContentWhenReady` and clears that timer as soon as headers return. After headers, only the Node stream remains — with no wall-clock — so a slow drip can keep `saveMediaStream` alive indefinitely.

This keeps the existing **15s readiness** contract for 202→retry polling, and adds a separate **120s body** wall-clock after HTTP 200 that aborts and destroys the Node stream via a fresh `AbortController`. Body budget matches Slack/Feishu inbound media totals (`SLACK_MEDIA_TOTAL_TIMEOUT_MS` / Feishu `120_000`) so late readiness still gets a full transfer window for the default 10MB cap. LINE documents `api-data.line.me` as the large-data content endpoint where video/audio may spend time preparing before binary retrieval.

The current `main` branch already uses `fetchWithRuntimeDispatcherOrMockedGlobal` (custom fetch + 202 polling) for LINE content download — this was introduced in #108351. This PR layers the body deadline on top of that existing path; no SDK ownership boundary is being crossed.

Non-goals: changing shared `saveMediaStream`, LINE send/API surfaces, or collapsing readiness+body into one shared 15s budget.

Collision check: no open PR on `extensions/line/src/download.ts`.

## User Impact

- Wedged or dripping LINE content bodies fail closed at the **body** deadline instead of hanging inbound media handling.
- Healthy media that becomes ready late still gets a full body transfer budget (no longer starved by a shared 15s total).
- Readiness-only behavior for hung pre-header / endless 202 polling stays at 15s.

## Evidence

Exact head: `4dcd73aee0e9c7178d0b55d2587a6a93c251cb90`

`oxfmt --check extensions/line/src/download.ts extensions/line/src/download.test.ts extensions/line/src/download.deadline.loopback.test.ts` — passed.
`git diff --check` — clean.

### Timeout contract

| Phase | Budget | Scope |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Readiness | `CONTENT_READY_TIMEOUT_MS` = 15s | 202 polling until HTTP 200 headers |
| Body | `LINE_MEDIA_BODY_TIMEOUT_MS` = 120s | `saveMediaStream` after headers; stream destroyed on abort |

### Tests

```bash
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/line/src/download.test.ts extensions/line/src/download.deadline.loopback.test.ts -- --run --reporter=verbose
```

```
 ✓ |extension-line| extensions/line/src/download.test.ts > downloadLineMedia > persists inbound media with the shared media store 229ms
 ✓ |extension-line| extensions/line/src/download.test.ts > downloadLineMedia > does not pass the external messageId to saveMediaStream 3ms
 ✓ |extension-line| extensions/line/src/download.test.ts > downloadLineMedia > cancels content when the media store rejects it 6ms
 ✓ |extension-line| extensions/line/src/download.test.ts > downloadLineMedia > uses media store content type for M4A media 2ms
 ✓ |extension-line| extensions/line/src/download.test.ts > downloadLineMedia > passes original filenames to the media store for extension fallback 4ms
 ✓ |extension-line| extensions/line/src/download.test.ts > downloadLineMedia > uses media store content type for MP4 video 2ms
 ✓ |extension-line| extensions/line/src/download.test.ts > downloadLineMedia > retries 202 responses and cancels every discarded body 4ms
 ✓ |extension-line| extensions/line/src/download.test.ts > downloadLineMedia > cancels every response when content never becomes ready 3ms
 ✓ |extension-line| extensions/line/src/download.test.ts > downloadLineMedia > cancels error responses without retrying 2ms
 ✓ |extension-line| extensions/line/src/download.test.ts > downloadLineMedia > aborts a hung content request at the readiness deadline 10ms
 ✓ |extension-line| extensions/line/src/download.test.ts > downloadLineMedia > aborts a dripping content body after headers within the body deadline 64ms
 ✓ |extension-line| extensions/line/src/download.test.ts > downloadLineMedia > keeps a fresh body deadline after late readiness 4ms
 ✓ |extension-line| extensions/line/src/download.deadline.loopback.test.ts > LINE media download wall-clock loopback > aborts a dripping content body within the body wall-clock deadline 567ms
 ✓ |extension-line| extensions/line/src/download.deadline.loopback.test.ts > LINE media download wall-clock loopback > persists a slow-but-valid body before the body deadline 96ms

 Test Files  2 passed (2)
      Tests  14 passed (14)
```

### Standalone loopback proof

Real `http.createServer` loopback + real `fetch` + real `Readable.fromWeb` + same AbortController body-deadline mechanism as `downloadLineMedia`. No vitest, no mock `saveMediaStream`, no fake timers.

```bash
HEAD_SHA=$(git rev-parse HEAD) node --import tsx proof-line-media-deadline.mts
```

```
--- Case 1: Dripping body aborts at wall-clock deadline ---
  info: error=LINE media body timed out after 0.25 seconds
  ok: dripping body rejects (does not drain)
  ok: error mentions body timed out
  ok: elapsed is near timeout (200-800ms)
  info: case=drip-body elapsed_ms=320 timeout_ms=250

--- Case 2: Slow body completes before deadline ---
  ok: slow body completes successfully
  ok: completed before deadline
  info: case=slow-ok elapsed_ms=108 total_bytes=5

--- Case 3: Negative control — idle-only reading stays unsettled ---
  ok: without wall-clock deadline, drip stays unsettled past 400ms
  info: case=negative-control outcome=still-pending elapsed_ms=436 settled=false

=== Summary ===
head=4dcd73aee0e9c7178d0b55d2587a6a93c251cb90
node=v22.22.0
ALL PROOF ASSERTIONS: 6 passed, 0 failed
```

- **Body drip (250ms timeout)**: 30ms continuous drip → stream destroyed in 320ms with "body timed out after 0.25 seconds" — wall-clock deadline bounds the body, not just headers.
- **Slow valid body (1500ms timeout)**: 100ms paced response → completes at 108ms with 5 bytes — healthy transfers not false-killed.
- **Negative control**: 30ms drip with no wall-clock bound → still pending at 436ms — proves the old code path has no wall-clock bound on the body.

### Not tested

Live `api-data.line.me` with LINE channel credentials — requires real LINE bot token.
